title: Auditor-ready compact trust brief for RBAC and SIEM
content:
- resource_id: GUID or canonical resource name
  - action: canonical action verb (create|read|update|delete|invoke|login|logout|grant|revoke)
  - outcome: success | failure | partial
  - client_ip: source IPv4/IPv6 when available
  - region: cloud region or datacenter id
  - latency_ms: optional for api.request/model.invoke
  - metadata: free-form map for context (prompt hashes, model version, quantization profile)

- Integrity and signing: Logs are stamped with sequence numbers and HMAC fingerprints for tamper-detection in hosted offerings; Dedicated/Private customers may configure forwarding from a local collector.
- Retention & export: Default retention 90 days hosted; Dedicated customers can set retention to match contractual SLAs. Exports allow time-bounded retrieval.

SIEM export patterns and delivery: (practical guidance)
- Formats: JSON-LD (preferred for structured ingestion), CEF for legacy tooling, and CSV for lightweight audits. Each record includes schema_version and event_type for mapping in the SIEM.
- Delivery mechanisms:
  1) Push: HTTPS webhook endpoint with mutual TLS and JWT for auth.
  2) Pull: S3-compatible bucket with per-export signed URL; customer-managed credentials optional.
  3) Forwarder: Lightweight collector (Docker/agent) customers run in their network to push logs into existing SIEM.
- Mapping examples:
  - Splunk: props/transforms JSON ingestion, recommended KV extraction on event_type and request_id.
  - Elastic: ingest pipeline with schema mapping; timestamp parse rule and keyword fields for facetting.
  - Datadog: forwarder uses JSON schema; recommended tags: role, actor_type, model_family, region.

Evidence automation and questionnaire workflow: (customer-facing)
- Evidence agent: A signed-runner process that bundles artifacts (policy definitions, role binding snapshots, retention configs, sample log extracts, export configs) into a verifiable evidence bundle. Bundles are signed and stored in the customer evidence store.
- Common evidence artifacts generated:
  - RBAC policy exports (current snapshot with version hash)
  - Immutable role-binding history (last 12 months)
  - Sample audit log slice anchored to request_ids referenced in questionnaire answers
  - SIEM export config and certificate thumbprints
  - Access review reports and MFA enforcement rollout logs
- Automation flows: Questionnaire template -> evidence mapping -> automated bundle request -> reviewer verifies and attaches to response. This reduces manual extractor time from days to hours.

Typical customer security questions (short responses and where to find evidence):
- Q: How do you enforce least privilege?
  A: RBAC v2 with least-privilege default roles and a policy DSL. Evidence: role snapshot + binding history (see evidence bundle id).
- Q: How are audit logs protected from tampering?
  A: HMAC sequencing and optional append-only storage in Dedicated; evidence: log integrity report + export hash.
- Q: Can we receive logs in our SIEM?
  A: Yes — push, pull, or forwarder patterns supported. Evidence: SIEM connector config and sample export.
- Q: Who approves role changes?
  A: Role changes require an approver chain defined in the policy; role_binding events record approver_id and justification. Evidence: role approval audit trail.

Operational notes for reviewers (internal):
- When assembling an evidence bundle for an external auditor, include: role snapshot, three representative log slices (auth, config change, model invoke), and SIEM connector verification artifact.
- Sanitize user identifiers when sharing publicly; provide mapping keys in a secure channel.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, coordinate with the customer's SRE to retrieve on-prem logs and include transport verification.

FAQ (short):
- Are custom roles allowed? Yes; customers can create custom roles within their namespace.
- Do we store full prompts in logs? No — we store prompt hashes and prompt metadata by default; full prompt capture is opt-in and logged as a sensitive event.
- How do we prove data deletion? We provide deletion receipts and retention policy snapshots in evidence bundles.

Next steps & recommended attachments for customer packet: (checklist)
- Attach: RBAC v2 policy snapshot (current)
- Attach: 90-day sample audit log slice (three categories)
- Attach: SIEM connector manifest and cert thumbprint
- Attach: evidence bundle manifest and signature
- Propose: 30-minute walkthrough call for auditors to demonstrate live SIEM export and role-binding UI

Appendix — short mapping to common controls (for auditor convenience):
- RBAC v2 -> CC6.2 / IAM controls: role definitions, separation of duties, privileged account reviews
- Audit log schema -> CC8.1 / Logging: tamper-evidence, correlation IDs, cross-service tracing
- SIEM export -> CC7.4 / Monitoring: integration with customer SIEM and alerting hooks
- Evidence automation -> CC9.3 / Evidence management: reproducible bundles, signed artifacts
